name: Denmark
snapshot: Mette Frederiksen's snap election backfired with her party's worst result in 120 years, but she clung on in a third government with Lars Løkke Rasmussen as kingmaker.
culture: Denmark exported hygge, the idea of cosy togetherness, as well as Lego, Danish design and Nordic noir TV. Cycling dominates Copenhagen. The monarchy is Europe's oldest, and King Frederik X succeeded his mother Margrethe in 2024. Hans Christian Andersen and Søren Kierkegaard are national icons.
society: Danes pay high taxes for a generous welfare state and are often ranked among the world's happiest people. Novo Nordisk, maker of Ozempic, became Europe's most valuable company. The Social Democrats adopted one of Europe's strictest immigration policies. Trump's demands to take over Greenland, part of the Danish realm, have dominated foreign policy.
situation: In January 2026, the president of the United States renewed his push to take Greenland, a semi-autonomous territory of the Danish kingdom, and refused to rule out force. Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen warned that an American takeover would mean the end of NATO, and Europe rallied behind her (Euronews). It was the most dramatic moment of her career, and she tried to turn it into a third term.

Frederiksen called a snap election for 24 March, months early. It backfired. Greenland barely featured, because Danes broadly agree on it, and the campaign turned on prices and welfare instead. Her Social Democrats had their worst result in 120 years, and her left-leaning bloc won 84 seats, short of the 90 needed for a majority (Al Jazeera). Her hard line on immigration had alienated left-wing voters without winning over the right. The kingmaker became Lars Løkke Rasmussen, her foreign minister and a former prime minister, whose centrist Moderates could swing either way. After weeks of talks, Frederiksen formed her third cabinet in early June. The four seats held by Greenland and the Faroe Islands, normally afterthoughts, briefly looked like they could decide who governed.
power: A constitutional monarchy with a parliamentary system. The prime minister needs the confidence of the 179-seat Folketing, including two members each from Greenland and the Faroe Islands; minority governments relying on deals across blocs are common. King Frederik X is head of state.
holders: Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen (Social Democrats), in her third government since June 2026.
